tools.name: convert_publisher_files
tools.description: Convert Microsoft Publisher (.pub) files to PDF, page images (PNG and JPG), ODG (editable in LibreOffice Draw) and text-only DOCX. Use it when the user has .pub files, or a .zip of them, that they want to open, view, print or convert. Pass public download links in file_urls, or files the user attach

tools.name: get_conversion
tools.description: Status of a conversion started with convert_publisher_files: each file's pages, warnings and watermarked preview images, the price, and pay_url. After the user has paid on aretus.app it also returns download_url, a ZIP of every converted file (valid for about an hour).

tools.name: get_free_file
tools.description: Get one converted file free and without watermark: a ZIP with its PDF, ODG, DOCX and page images. Limited to one free file per email address and one per batch. It needs the user's own email address: ask the user for it and use it only with their agreement, never an address they did not give for this

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Prices and limits of the Aretus Publisher (.pub) converter: the one-time price by number of converted files, what is free, file size limits and how long files are kept.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_free_file · Private data: convert_publisher_files, get_conversion, get_free_file, get_pricing · Public sink: convert_publisher_files, get_free_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_free_file · Private data: convert_publisher_files, get_conversion, get_free_file, get_pricing · Public sink: convert_publisher_files, get_free_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
